meta.note: Every published plenary journal read from its PDF text layer: what each sitting did, every measure it acted on, the substance of debate, and recorded votes. Measures are named as the journal prints them; a proposed resolution carries its adopted number only where the journal or Parliament's index confirms it. BTA1 and BTA2 numbered their bills separately, so a BTA1 bill is linked only through the act it became.

journals.title: Journal No. 1 of March 29, 2019 Plenary Session
journals.presiding: Interim Chief Minister Ahod B. Ebrahim, then Speaker Ali Pangalian M. Balindong

absent: MP Haroun Alrashid A. Lucman, Jr.
MP Rolan Abdul Rashid A. Macarambon
attendance.note: 92 Members present at the roll call; 7 noted absent. The Wali, Sheikh Khalipa Usman Nando, took his oath and opened the First Regular Session.

journals.summary: The inaugural sitting of 29 March 2019 adopted the Rules of the Parliament for the election of officers, subject to later amendment, and elected Ali Pangalian M. Balindong Speaker by viva voce over Laisa M. Alamia, who was declared Minority Floor Leader. Hatimil E. Hassan (Deputy Speaker), Lanang T. Ali, Jr. (Majority Floor Leader), Raby B. Angkal (Secretary General) and Abdulgani B. Caludtiag (Sergeant-at-Arms) were elected as lone nominees. The body then adopted Proposed Resolutions No. 1 to 4, on the Wali, condolences for MP Ghazali B. Jaafar, and the transition and ARMM funds.

journals.summary: The sitting of 22 May 2019 adopted the session calendar (Proposed Resolution No. 15) and read BTA Parliament Bill No. 3, on Cotabato City as the permanent seat of government, on first reading. It elected MP Eduard U. Guerra chair of the Committee on Finance, Budget and Management and confirmed its members. items.text: Withdrawn by its authors, MP Eduard Guerra and MP Ubaida Pacasem.
Deputy Chief Minister Abdul Sahrin delivered a privilege speech, attached as Appendix B and made part of the Journal.
MP Eddie Alih spoke on the urgent need to activate and constitute the Intergovernmental Relations Body of the Bangsamoro Government; referred to the Committee on Rules.
MP Mussolini Lidasan called for the creation of a BARMM Inter-Agency Financial Audit Committee; referred to the Committee on Rules.

points.point: The Chair asked whether Proposed Resolution No. 62 amends the Parliamentary Rules; MP Lanang Ali Jr. answered that Section 5, Rule VI allows a resolution defining the regular session, so it amends the earlier calendar.
MP Amilbahar Mawallil asked about the 21 August resumption date falling on a holiday; MP Lanang Ali Jr. said a session day that falls on a holiday moves to the next day, 22 August.
MP Laisa Alamia proposed adding a sentence that the resolution nullifies the previous calendar of session; the author accepted.
MP Khadafeh Mangudadatu moved to treat Proposed Resolution No. 42 as a simple resolution for the Business for the Day.
MP Anna Tarhata Basman appealed for thorough deliberation instead, saying the subject is more than an expression of sentiment.
The Majority Floor Leader said the referral stands because the question of postponing barangay elections needs the Chief Minister's attention; MP Mangudadatu then adhered to the referral.
MP Laisa Alamia said the Zones of Joint Cooperation follow the 1982 UNCLOS and Section 18, Article XIII of RA 11054, and the Joint Body should have convened within 30 days of ratification.

MP Omar Yasser Sema joined the MNLF members as co-authors and moved to consolidate Proposed Resolution Nos. 52 and 55 and add the Moro Gulf to the title; MP Amilbahar Mawallil, for the proponents, agreed and the motion carried.

MP Amilbahar Mawallil raised a point of order that the sponsorship speech should precede referral; the Majority Floor Leader explained that under the Rules sponsorship comes on Second Stage, and promised to take the concern to the Committee on Rules.

MP Anna Tarhata Basman, who had not signed the committee report, asked why Marawi and Lamitan are folded into their provinces while Cotabato City gets its own ray; MP Lanang Ali Jr. said the wording follows the CAB and RA 11054 and that Cotabato City has always been independent.
MP Anna Tarhata Basman insisted it was a matter of equity, noting the 3 cities have no separate representation in the House of Representatives.

MP Paisalin Tago argued that if the CAB and BOL do not describe the flag the body may amend it, and appealed for a separate ray for Marawi, citing the Dansalan Declaration and its status as the only Islamic City.
MP Romeo Saliga asked where the Indigenous Peoples and settler communities appear in the proposed flag.
MP Abdullah Macapaar asked for a ray representing Muslims outside the BARMM, including Lanao del Norte, and said he would otherwise propose a new design.
Speaker Ali Pangalian Balindong explained the order of committee and individual amendments before second-reading voting, then moved to defer the bill given the objections; approved.
MP Khadafeh Mangudadatu asked whether the Arabic version of the emblem is also official; MP Lanang Ali Jr. said both are official because English and Arabic are the official languages of the BARMM.

journals.summary: Over 2 days the Parliament welcomed new MPs Ziaur-Rahman Alonto Adiong and Diamila Ramos, referred 6 proposed resolutions, and moved Proposed Resolution Nos. 70, 84 and 85 to the Business for the Day as simple resolutions. items.text: On motion of MP Adzfar Usman, the Secretary-General was asked to arrange the ceremonial signing by the Chief Minister of the first parliamentary act, on the BARMM Flag, approved the previous week.

points.point: MP Jose Lorena objected to the word 'enhancements' in the title, saying the body should not breach parliamentary courtesy with the House of Representatives and the Senate.
MP Ziaur-Rahman Alonto Adiong seconded treating it as a simple resolution so debate could open and amendments be introduced.

MP Eduard Guerra explained that DBM approved funding for members' staff only from 1 August 2019, so the 2019 GAA allocation for regional assemblymen whose terms ended 30 June 2019 would be realigned to pay staff for July 2019.
MP Suharto Ambolodto asked whether an appropriation can be realigned by a simple resolution; the Majority Floor Leader said passage is needed to comply with a DBM requirement.
MP Ziaur-Rahman Alonto Adiong argued that if the body can allocate national funds it can also realign them, since some staff depend on their salaries.

MP Abdulraof Macacua asked for a report every session on the status of proposed resolutions referred to the Committee on Rules; MP Suharto Ambolodto and the Chair backed the call for the committee to act on them.
MP Paisalin Tago asked whether the Director-General equals the old ARMM post; MP Alzad Sattar said no, the former post was Undersecretary for the Bureau of Madaris Education.
MP Maisara Dandamun-Latiph said 2% of the block grant is only a minimum, about ₱1.4 billion of a ₱70 billion grant, and not enough for a good Madrasah system.
MP Jose Lorena asked whether the bill was discussed with the Minister of Education drafting the Education Code; MP Alzad Sattar said consultants told him it is aligned.

MP Ziaur-Rahman Alonto Adiong asked whether asatidz rules should wait for the Bangsamoro Civil Service Code; MP Alzad Sattar described the DepEd qualifying exam and the 1-year ATEP program for ALIVE teachers.
Minister Mohagher Iqbal said the Education Code being drafted covers Madaris, so the bill should simply be referred to committee.

MP Eddie Alih noted Section 18, Article IX of RA 11054 requires coordination with DepEd, CHED and TESDA and said it appeared none was made before filing; MP Alzad Sattar replied members have the right to file any bill.
MP Suharto Ambolodto asked whether the Office for Settler Communities would have regulatory powers; MP Susana Anayatin said yes.
MP Sahie Udjah supported the hymn but suggested it be sung in Filipino or Tagalog.
MP Romeo Saliga asked to present the hymn to Indigenous Peoples for comment so it reflects all peoples; MP Romeo Sema called the request well taken.
MP Baintan Ampatuan suggested public consultation and a chorus for male and female singers.
MP Eddie Alih asked whether the melody is original; MP Romeo Sema said yes.
MP Basit Abbas suggested the hymn be sung in every tribal dialect of the Bangsamoro.
MP Abdulmuhmin Mujahid objected that 'Hukuma' in the Arabic version means government, though the region is only autonomous, and said the Ulama he consulted did not accept the translation.
MP Mohagher Iqbal said the literal Arabic is not correct, proposed review by Arabic and English grammarians, and moved to table discussion of the Arabic translation.
MP Sahie Udjah warned the Arabic version implies political independence while the English version says autonomous region.

MP Lanang Ali Jr. said the body would approve the English version and could correct the Arabic later; MP Ziaur-Rahman Alonto Adiong suggested putting the Arabic beneath the English to have only 1 official seal.
MP Hamid Aminoddin Barra agreed 'Hukumah' makes the Arabic questionable and proposed changing the Arabic text.
MP Omar Yasser Sema, citing the urgency of a seal for IDs and business cards, moved to adopt only the English version; accepted by the sponsor.

MP Raissa Jajurie was the sole nominee for Deputy Majority Floor Leader after a contested nomination was withdrawn, and MP Suharto Ambolodto became Deputy Minority Floor Leader by consensus. Debate on No. 70 turned on whether the Parliament should commend congressmen for filing bills.

points.point: MP Jose Lorena said the BTA already has power to create municipalities and the proponents should file a bill for the Committee on Local Government instead of a resolution directing the BTA.
The Majority Floor Leader said the resolution was meant to trigger discussion of the many petitions from the 63 barangays in North Cotabato.
MP Nabil Tan asked why a bill was not filed directly, and MP Ziaur-Rahman Alonto Adiong added that a resolution is not a prerequisite to a bill and the priority codes should come first.
MP Omar Yasser Sema said he had already prepared a bill creating a municipality from the 63 barangays and joined as co-author.
MP Maisara Dandamun-Latiph urged referral without delay and assured that the Local Government Code would treat the 63 barangays as part of BARMM territory.
MP Nabil Tan asked whether the ₱100 million would come from the block grant; MP Rasul Ismael said no, it is a Senate commitment to be charged to the 2020 GAA.

MP Musa Diamla said ₱100 million may not be enough and asked that the amount follow the technical computation; the Majority Floor Leader said it was not a good idea to ask the Senate for more than it offered.
MP Jose Lorena suggested asking Senator Migz Zubiri for a continuing ₱1 billion budget for the building, starting with the ₱100 million offered.

MP Ziaur-Rahman Alonto Adiong asked whether the deputy floor leader positions must be created before members are elected; the Chair said the positions were already created, and MP Adiong said he had no objection.

MP Ziaur-Rahman Alonto Adiong proposed adding House Bill Nos. 3428 and 3922 to the sixth Whereas clause; the author accepted, but MP Adiong later withdrew it and moved to drop the clause naming bill authors.
MP Paisalin Tago objected that commending congressmen for filing a bill is inappropriate since it is their duty, and warned of setting a precedent.
MP Eddie Alih defended recognizing congressmen whose bills help Marawi siege victims and moved for division of the house if the objection stood.
MP Hamid Aminoddin Barra proposed rewording the title to 'expressing support to the filing' so the body would not be commending the filer.
MP Alzad Sattar said members should first ask what the people have felt from the BTA's work in 6 months, saying his inbox is full of complaints.
Speaker Ali Pangalian Balindong moved approval subject to style without naming the House bill authors; MP Paisalin Tago subscribed and the motion carried.
MP Omar Yasser Sema objected to approval subject to style because funding already allotted to an office cannot be realigned by mere resolution.
MP Baintan Ampatuan suggested retitling it as a resolution authorizing use of personal services funds for BTA staff, noting a bill is needed to realign.
The Chair asked what the source of funds was and how much would be allotted; with the authors absent, consideration was deferred.

points.point: MP Abdulmuhmin Mujahid moved to withdraw Proposed Resolution No. 43, saying the military in Cotabato City had already acted on it.
MP Omar Yasser Sema noted checkpoints remain in Sultan Kudarat and south of the city and suggested amending it to cover all checkpoints in and out of Cotabato City and Maguindanao.

MP Jose Lorena objected to the withdrawal, warning the arrangement with the police may be temporary and the AFP and PNP must respect the BTA; MP Hamid Aminoddin Barra and MP Sahie Udjah joined, Barra noting the clearance covers MPs but not staff.
MP Paisalin Tago asked whether an objector to a withdrawal must file a substitute resolution; MP Abdulmuhmin Mujahid then withdrew his motion to withdraw.

MP Eddie Alih and MP Punduma Sani asked to extend coverage to Zamboanga City, Lanao del Sur and other BARMM areas, and MP Maisara Latiph proposed addressing it to martial law administrator Secretary Delfin Lorenzana.
MP Maisara Latiph asked to co-author, saying electricity is also a human right.
MP Jose Lorena suggested widening the inquiry to the electric cooperatives in the BARMM, and MP Nabil Tan and MP Eddie Alih to other provinces as far as Tawi-Tawi.
MP Omar Yasser Sema suggested referral to a Committee on Energy; the Chair said that committee is not yet created, so the Committee on Rules would refer it.
MP Susana Anayatin asked that the inquiry also look into why power in the BARMM is the most expensive in the country.
Deputy Minister Zul Qarneyn M. Abas reported 2,516 suspected dengue cases from 1 January to 13 August, about twice the same period last year, with 22 deaths and a 0.9% case fatality rate.
MP Laisa Alamia asked for the provincial breakdown; MP Abas cited Maguindanao 985, Lanao del Sur 712 and Marawi 407, and agreed fresh-water areas are most affected.
MP Laisa Alamia asked the Ministry of Health to study the causes of the 22 deaths; MP Abas said the deaths were in hospitals from complications.
On the dengue vaccine, MP Abas said many academic doctors do not recommend it and that 200 plus policemen vaccinated through DOH-ARMM are being monitored, with no deaths reported.

MP Omar Yasser Sema asked about readiness and funding; MP Abas said many programs are unfunded and gave 16 billion as the ideal initial figure, which could be toned down (the journal later refers to it as 16 million pesos).
MP Musa Diamla asked the Ministry of Health to include completion and operation of the unfinished Marawi City Public Hospital in its plans.

points.point: MP Zul Qarneyn Abas asked the intent of the resolution and MP Ziaur-Rahman Adiong raised a point of order that referral should not be debated; the Chair ruled the Rules let a proponent explain the general purpose on first reading.
MP Romeo C. Saliga said development projects were entering Indigenous Peoples' areas without consultation and creating conflicts on the ground.

Speaker Ali Pangalian Balindong asked whether BASAC adds bureaucracy under the Office of the Chief Minister; MP Omar Yasser Sema said yes, an advisory office focused only on poverty, as many ministries are not dedicated to it.
MP Jose Lorena warned the bill could overload the BARMM bureaucracy and make it an employment agency, citing the 33,000 ARMM employees.
MP Eddie Alih said the 15 ministries are more than enough to advise the Chief Minister on poverty and kept his reservation.
Deputy Chief Minister Abdul Sahrin said poverty is driven by graft and corruption and suggested an anti-corruption agency like Malaysia's.

MP Baintan Ampatuan noted BASAC is not a BOL priority and asked why not fund programs directly for poor communities instead of an office; MP Sema said the bill aims to act against poverty, not eradicate it overnight.
MP Maisara D. Latiph asked to co-author and proposed 12 commissioners from marginalized sectors so the body takes a bottom-up approach.
MP Baintan A. Ampatuan asked which pacts and covenants would be recognized, saying approving without knowing them would adopt something blank; the Chair asked for copies.
MP Romeo C. Saliga cited a yearly pact between the Irumanan Manubo and Moro communities in Carmen, North Cotabato, and the Mamalu-Tabunaway 'sawit' exchange.
The Majority Floor Leader backed the resolution but advised replacing 'Muslim Filipino' with 'Moro' for consistency with 'Non-Moro Indigenous People'.
MP Zul Qarneyn M. Abas called for an enumeration and comprehensive review of the pacts to see if they still apply.
MP Laisa M. Alamia said pacts, treaties and covenants carry legal implications that must be reviewed before recognition.
MP Datu Tucao O. Mastura said unwritten pacts cannot legally be considered but urged the body to recognize the Tedurays as Bangsamoro.
MP Sittie Shahara I. Mastura said some local chief executives were widening roads, treating 15 meters from the highway center as right of way, which requires compensation.
The Majority Floor Leader cited DILG Secretary Año that Memorandum Circular 2019-121 covers only road obstructions and not road widening.
MP Baintan A. Ampatuan asked whether the circular was officially received by the BARMM or only circulated on Facebook, saying the BARMM is not bound otherwise.
MP Suharto M. Ambolodto asked that a Committee on Local Government look into acts already done in good faith by local officials.
MP Paisalin P. Tago said House Resolution No. 333 was unnecessary because the BOL already provides the Intergovernmental Relations mechanism, and the BTA must protect autonomy.
MP Jose I. Lorena called it an anathema to meaningful autonomy contrary to Section 6, Article VI and Section 37, Article XIII of RA 11054, and said he would go to court against any such law.
Deputy Speaker Hatimil E. Hassan noted RA 11054 created a Ministry of Public Works without Highways and that the 2020 national budget has more than ₱5 billion for highways in the BARMM.
MP Don Mustapha A. Loong argued the national DPWH must have offices in the region because the BOL makes it responsible for the 992 kilometers of national roads.
MP Laisa M. Alamia noted the resolution did not follow the 3-day notice rule and cited Disomangcop v. Datumanong on DPWH field offices.
OIC Chief Minister Abdulraof A. Macacua read a text from Congressman Mujiv Hataman saying the House authors were allies, proposed a meeting first, and later abstained.

rollCalls.note: Division of the house by standing, not a name-by-name roll. The first count was 41 in favor and 10 against; after MP Romeo K. Sema and OIC Chief Minister Abdulraof A. Macacua said they had abstained, a second count gave 40 in favor, 9 against and 7 abstentions. The Speaker did not vote. No names are recorded.

Under Other Matters, Minister of Finance Eduard U. Guerra said the Chief Minister expected to submit the 2020 Bangsamoro budget proposal in the fourth week of October; MP Maisara D. Latiph's call to activate a Committee on Justice was noted.

points.point: MP Omar Yasser C. Sema said many people had come to his office for affidavits to prove their identity and urgently need official IDs, particularly in Cotabato City.
MP Omar Yasser C. Sema cited 3 bombings involving foreign nationals and said PSA IDs would also help identify voters under the Electoral Code being drafted.
The Majority Floor Leader said the NCIP Region XII survey covers 201,880 hectares, 80% of Maguindanao, and that only the Ministry of Indigenous Peoples' Affairs has jurisdiction in the BARMM.

MP Romeo C. Saliga, for the non-Moro Indigenous Peoples, said approval would deny them ancestral domain rights under the Constitution, IPRA and RA 11054, and moved that the NCIP and claimants be invited to explain.
MP Romeo C. Saliga said titled and government properties, roughly 50%, would be excluded from the 201,880 hectares, leaving far less for the ancestral domain.
MP Khadafeh G. Mangudadatu agreed with the proponents but suggested softening the word 'protesting' in the title, and joined as co-author.
MP Jamel D. Macaraya and MP Maisara D. Latiph said the NCIP move runs against the BOL and should go through the Intergovernmental Relations Body, Latiph citing the 200,000 hectares involved.
MP Don Mustapha A. Loong said an official BTA website would spare members trips to the Secretary-General's office for copies of resolutions, bills and session schedules.
MP Ziaur-Rahman A. Adiong asked whether a budget is needed; MP Loong said no, it would be charged to the Secretary-General's Management Information System Unit.
MP Jose I. Lorena urged allocating funds to keep up with information technology; MP Loong declined to set a precedent of budget items in a simple resolution, pointing to the 2020 budget.
MP Nabil A. Tan asked whether the BTA has expert technicians; MP Loong said the hardware is procured and the website is 80% done.
MP Saffrullah M. Dipatuan said the BARMM must communicate its accomplishments after 7 months and asked to co-author.

items.text: The Majority Floor Leader reported that membership of the Committee on Accounts was being finalized with the Minority, which had submitted 2 names.

points.point: MP Mohagher M. Iqbal said the resolution was good but noted the issue was already being discussed in the intergovernmental relations bodies of the BARMM and the National Government.

MP Jose I. Lorena objected that a separate NCIP–MIPA dialogue would dilute the intergovernmental relations mechanism under RA 11054, which he said is the sole body to settle national–Bangsamoro differences.

MP Ali B. Sangki voiced reservations about non-Moro ancestral domain claims, saying over 2,000,000 hectares had been awarded under CADTs and that NCIP claims overlapped earlier presidential Muslim settlements.

MP Ali B. Sangki asked about the membership of the Committee on Indigenous Peoples' Affairs, warning against referral to a body with no Muslim members; the Majority Floor Leader undertook to give him the list.
MP Baintan A. Ampatuan noted that Proposed Resolutions No. 230 and No. 231 were worded the same; the Majority Floor Leader said they were referred to different committees.

MP Paisalin P. Tago proposed consolidating the 2 resolutions for joint committee hearings instead of reconsidering the referrals, the author MP Maisara D. Latiph agreed, and MP Ziaur-Rahman Alonto Adiong withdrew his motion to reconsider.

The Majority Floor Leader did not accept MP Jose I. Lorena's amendments to Section 5 (a Chairman and 6 Commissioners representing all geographic units) and Section 6 (7-year terms appointed by the Chief Minister).
MP Rasol Y. Mitmug, Jr.'s amendments making sports a tool for peace and transitional justice in Section 4 and item 9 were accepted.
MP Ziaur-Rahman Alonto Adiong asked how terms like transitional justice would be defined; the Majority Floor Leader said MP Maisara D. Latiph would propose a definition-of-terms section.
MP Diamila D. Ramos's amendment on a Sports Advisory Council of ministries, LGUs and sector representatives was not accepted after comparison with the original provision.
MP Bai Maleiha B. Candao protested that as author she was ignored; the Chair said proponents not physically present may not defend their measures, per an agreement among Members.
MP Jose I. Lorena's amended title, expressing the BTA's deep concern over the killings, was accepted by MP Aida M. Silongan and her co-author.
Sponsor MP Lanang T. Ali, Jr. said House Bill No. 6413 had passed the House but was pending in the Senate, which reportedly had not given it time.

MP Paisalin P. Tago questioned the names Northern and Southern Maguindanao, citing the cultural split after Lanao's division, and recorded a very big reservation; MP Khadafeh G. Mangudadatu said the south would have 25 municipalities and the north the 11 of the First District.
MP Ali B. Sangki suggested incorporating the 63 BARMM barangays in North Cotabato into the 2 new provinces, raising the total from 508 to 571 barangays, citing Ligawasan Marsh.
MP Nabil A. Tan asked why the Senate was not named and warned Congress might read the resolution as saying it had acted slowly.

points.point: MP Khadafeh G. Mangudadatu said every municipality in Maguindanao already had isolation facilities and suggested the resolution instead ask the regional government to fund equipment for them.

MP Jose I. Lorena asked whether Congress had created the hospital and why it was not funded; MP Paisalin P. Tago said the Regional Legislative Assembly created it and gave initial funding from former ARMM local funds.
MP Suharto M. Ambolodto worried about using a resolution to operationalize a law and asked the body to consider whether that was proper.
MP Ali B. Sangki said the Iranun District Hospital had been found dilapidated but was now operating on provincial funds, and urged funding for the Buluan and Shariff Aguak district hospitals too.
MP Amilbahar S. Mawallil objected that manifestations during referral pre-empt committee discussion and should not be entertained absent an objection.
MP Punduma B. Sani supported the resolution but said the term rebel returnee had been abused since the 1976 Tripoli Agreement and stated that he, an MNLF member, had never surrendered.

MP Baintan A. Ampatuan asked about existing OWWA data and cautioned that uploading the data online might breach the Data Privacy Law; MP Bai Maleiha B. Candao said nothing endangering workers would be released.
MP Bai Maleiha B. Candao said official data showed 50,000 Overseas Bangsamoro Workers in 2020 but illegal recruitment meant the true number was higher.

Asked by MP Jose I. Lorena, MP Romeo K. Sema said migrant workers were under the Ministry of Labor and Employment but recruitment agencies were not yet accredited due to COVID-19, and OWWA/POEA data-sharing was before a DOLE–MOLE working group.
MP Jose I. Lorena asked how much the data banking system would cost; the author had no estimate and would refer it to the Ministry.

MP Jamel D. Macaraya asked whether migrant overseas workers covers overseas workers, which the author confirmed, and signaled an amendment; MP Said M. Sheik backed the measure citing 25 years in Saudi Arabia.

journals.summary: Over 2 days, the Parliament approved Committee Substitute Bill No. 52 creating the Bangsamoro Sports Commission on second reading after the Committee on Rules folded in the amendments. It debated Parliament Bill No. 36 on Overseas Bangsamoro Workers at length over jurisdiction and lack of consultation with national agencies, then recommitted it. measure.titleAsRead: AN ACT CREATING BANGSAMORO SPORTS COMMISSION, PROVIDING FOR ITS MANDATE, POWERS, AND FUNCTIONS, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

items.text: Approved unanimously on second reading by viva voce voting.

points.point: MP Nabil A. Tan asked whether committee amendments were in the report and said salary grades should match those of other commissions the Parliament created.
MP Amilbahar S. Mawallil asked what procedure applies to a recommitted bill, the first in the Parliament; the Chair said it had been recommitted for the Committee on Rules to review the amendments.
MP Paisalin P. Tago and MP Jose I. Lorena argued no further floor amendments were needed since individual amendments had been submitted to the Committee on Rules for incorporation.

MP Ziaur-Rahman Alonto Adiong asked whether Section 25's appropriation would be charged to the current or the 2021 budget; MP Paisalin P. Tago said initial funding was already certified by the Finance Minister.
The Majority Floor Leader said funds were certified from the Contingency Fund of the 2020 budget, with more to be requested once staffing was complete.

MP Baintan A. Ampatuan said the Section 12 structure put the Commission proper and divisions on the same level and omitted the Executive Director; her amendments to fold the divisions under the Secretariat were captured in the final draft.

MP Jose I. Lorena and MP Paisalin P. Tago objected to defining repatriation as returning a person 'to its owner', since no one owns a person; MP Paisalin P. Tago proposed 'to the place of origin or citizenship'.
Asked by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan, MP Romeo K. Sema said the costly item was Bangsamoro Help Desks in Philippine embassies, which could be piloted in 1 country during the transition.

MP Nabil A. Tan doubted that prosecutorial powers could be given to the Ministry of Labor and Employment without the Department of Justice and noted Shari'ah courts' criminal jurisdiction is limited to minor cases.

MP Ziaur-Rahman Alonto Adiong questioned charging the ₱10,000,000 repatriation and reintegration fund to the Block Grant, saying it pre-empted the Committee on Finance; MP Romeo K. Sema said it had not been raised with that committee.

MP Raissa H. Jajurie warned that legislating rights for Bangsamoro workers outside the region could take jurisdiction from OWWA, POEA and DOLE and leave non-Bangsamoro workers without equal protection.

MP Laisa M. Alamia, a former overseas worker, asked whether funds should augment existing national assistance rather than set up help desks abroad and urged a review for conflicts with DFA, DOLE and OWWA laws.
MP Omar Yasser C. Sema established that DOJ, DOLE and DFA had not been consulted; MP Romeo K. Sema said the law did not require consultation with the National Government.

MP Maisara D. Latiph raised a point of order that the Rules make consultation discretionary ('may'); MP Amilbahar S. Mawallil replied that agencies with jurisdiction had still not been consulted, and the bill was recommitted.

MP Maisara D. Latiph, who signed with reservation, said the 127-page report failed to record the IDPs' own words on Kambalingan (homecoming) and wrongly stated the BTA has no control over the Marawi LGU, citing the constitutional liberty of abode.

MP Zul Qarneyn M. Abas asked how the proposed project management office or coordinating committee would relate to Task Force Bangon Marawi; MP Anna Tarhata S. Basman said the relationship would be coordinative and collaborative.
MP Diamila D. Ramos said only 20% to 30% of IDPs allowed to return had done so for lack of resources to rebuild, and urged support for her Proposed Resolution No. 130 on financial assistance.
MP Musa K.S. Diamla, a Ground Zero IDP, said Kambalingan was addressed on page 13 of the report and commended Task Force Bangon Marawi.

MP Laisa M. Alamia said land, housing and property issues must be resolved and moved to transmit the report to the Government of the Day, which MP Paisalin P. Tago and MP Nabil A. Tan amended to add national and local recipients.
Asked by MP Paisalin P. Tago what immediate assistance was possible, sponsor MP Amilbahar S. Mawallil hoped the Government of the Day would allot special funds or immediate cash aid.

measure.titleAsRead: AN ACT CREATING BANGSAMORO SPORTS COMMISSION, PROVIDING FOR ITS MANDATE, POWERS, AND FUNCTIONS, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES

items.text: Approved on third and final reading by nominal voting, 54 in favor, 0 against, 0 abstentions.

points.point: MP Baintan A. Ampatuan asked about the status of the Ministry of Public Order and Safety investigation to avoid duplication; MP Mohagher M. Iqbal said Minister Hussein P. Muñoz was in Davao and had tested positive for COVID-19.

MP Romeo K. Sema said the Chief Minister had already created an investigation team led by the Ministry and proposed retitling the resolution to support it so Parliament and the Chief Minister would not hold 2 positions.

Author MP Paisalin P. Tago replied that a Bangsamoro investigation could be called biased after its condemnation statement and that the Bangsamoro Government had no jurisdiction over those involved outside BARMM.
MP Mohagher M. Iqbal urged separating facts from allegations, citing reports that Muslims and Christians were sorted and the Muslims killed.

MP Raissa H. Jajurie objected to the motion to approve, saying the Ministry's draft report had already gone to the Office of the Chief Minister; the Chair said the resolution concerned the NBI, PNP and CHR, not the Ministry.
MP Jose I. Lorena amended the title to urge the PNP, NBI, CHR and Cotabato provincial government to investigate and bring the perpetrators to justice; MP Paisalin P. Tago accepted.

MP Amilbahar S. Mawallil voted yes but asked for improvement in the process; he later questioned which rule allows Members to become co-authors after third reading, and the Majority Floor Leader said it was a courtesy the Rules do not prohibit.

rollCalls.note: Nominal voting on third and final reading; 54 in favor, none against and no abstention, as printed. MP Suharto M. Ambolodto, MP Datu Tucao O. Mastura and MP Amilbahar S. Mawallil explained their votes.

points.point: MP Aida M. Silongan said months after the killing authorities had reported no action, and urged action so Bangsamoro outside BARMM would not feel forgotten.
MP Bainon G. Karon said the body of a 14-year-old Moro girl was found on 14 September 2020 in a river in Barangay Malanduague, Kabacan, after she went to gather firewood.

MP Baintan A. Ampatuan asked whether a police investigation was not already standard procedure and whether the Bangsamoro Women Commission had been briefed; MP Bainon G. Karon said the Executive Secretary told her an investigation was ongoing.
MP Paisalin P. Tago, told that Kabacan police had filed no case because of the time element, said police should file on the strength of the corpus delicti and blotter even without a complainant.

MP Jamel D. Macaraya said there was no formal Bangsamoro investigation and proposed a fact-finding team; MP Khadafeh G. Mangudadatu wanted committee referral, while MP Ziaur-Rahman Alonto Adiong said that would defeat the call for urgency.
MP Paisalin P. Tago said Jikiri, Chief of Staff of the Bangsamoro Armed Forces, was a pillar of the MNLF whose sacrifices deserved recognition; MP Nabil A. Tan called him a man of peace.
Asked by MP Nabil A. Tan, MP Jose I. Lorena said 2025 was chosen to synchronize with national elections and that normalization, including the Normalization Trust Fund, had not been implemented.
MP Jose I. Lorena agreed with MP Nabil A. Tan that an extension would not guarantee reappointment of current Members, as appointment is the President's prerogative.

MP Nabil A. Tan asked whether a real assessment of BARMM was needed as a basis rather than a civil society report; MP Jose I. Lorena said he relied on the Chief Minister's statement that MILF communities had not been rehabilitated.

MP Omar Yasser C. Sema called the title vague and drew from MP Jose I. Lorena that elections would be postponed and that the region was not ready for 2022 elections because of the pandemic; he asked evidence be annexed for 2 whereas clauses.

MP Edrieza H.N. Rimbang asked whether the sponsor was the Chief Minister's counsel and whether Members had consulted the President or the people; MP Jose I. Lorena said he stood on his own and cited 'salus populi est suprema lex'.

MP Mohagher M. Iqbal said the extension was not self-serving: the MILF sought 7 years, the draft law 5, but the Organic Law gave 3, and the Normalization Trust Fund was unfunded and decommissioning's second phase unmet.
MP Paisalin P. Tago urged passage even though AFP Chief of Staff Gilbert Gapay had retracted his statement on madaris, as a reference for future officials.

MP Bai Maleiha B. Candao attributed the issue to a communication gap and urged dialogue between the AFP chief and Islamic leaders; MP Hamid Aminoddin D. Barra suggested asking the AFP to study Islam as a religion of peace.
MP Omar Yasser C. Sema proposed toning down the language since the MILF and MNLF are now partners of the Government; the Chair agreed.

points.point: MP Romeo K. Sema said a DOJ representative confirmed but did not attend, so the penalties were not discussed, and stressed the Ministry only assists the DOJ in prosecution.
MP Ziaur-Rahman Alonto Adiong asked why the bill was not a Cabinet bill given its funding needs; MP Romeo K. Sema said it was filed as a private bill but fits the Chief Minister's 12-point agenda.
MP Nabil A. Tan raised a point of order asking whether the issues for which the bill was recommitted had been put to the DOJ and DFA, and what the bill's status was after recommittal.
MP Romeo K. Sema told MP Jose I. Lorena no new provisions were added since agencies did not attend, and said POEA preferred help desks in Philippine Overseas Labor Offices rather than embassies.
MP Baintan A. Ampatuan noted 6 different terms for the workers covered, only 3 defined, and asked the basis for the ₱10,000,000 repatriation fund and whether the ₱5,000,000 legal fund was enough.

MP Raissa H. Jajurie proposed dropping 'outside the Bangsamoro territory' from the coverage and instead letting the Ministry extend assistance, warning that mandatory jurisdiction would burden workers living far from its offices.
MP Suharto M. Ambolodto asked whether Section 46 on an Overseas Bangsamoro Workers' Day was a rider not germane to the title.
MP Laisa M. Alamia proposed wording the penal provisions to refer expressly to RA 8042 so national amendments carry over; the sponsor agreed.
MP Jose I. Lorena said jurisdictional issues between the Ministry and national agencies remained unresolved; the Majority Floor Leader moved a technical working group, which was created.

MP Lanang T. Ali, Jr. objected that cutting the Secretary-General from salary grade 29 to 28 mid-term was a diminution, noting Congress secretaries-general match legislators; MP Anna Tarhata S. Basman said the committee did not want it equal to Members.
MP Lanang T. Ali, Jr. and MP Maisara D. Latiph objected to placing the Administrative and Finance office under the Speaker rather than the Secretary-General.
Asked by MP Paisalin P. Tago, MP Anna Tarhata S. Basman said positions would rise from the former Regional Legislative Assembly's 276 to 1,215, an increase of 939.
MP Paisalin P. Tago and MP Romeo C. Saliga sought more staff for legislative research and translation, including sign language and live interpretation.

MP Jose I. Lorena said he might file a Parliamentary Service Act converting the Secretary-General into a Clerk of the Parliament; MP Nabil A. Tan backed the idea and called the structure a hybrid of unitary and parliamentary models.
MP Bai Maleiha B. Candao supported restoring the Secretary-General's salary grade, citing the Secretariat's work through the pandemic.

points.point: MP Paisalin P. Tago explained that the extension of accountable officers would expire on 31 December 2020 and that without a further extension the operations of offices would be paralyzed, with about 57 accountable officers in Parliament and an estimated 100 in all.

MP Amilbahar S. Mawallil asked whether 'Bangsamoro Transition Authority' meant only Parliament; MP Tago answered that it refers to the whole interim Bangsamoro Government under Article XVI of the Bangsamoro Organic Law.

MP Baintan A. Ampatuan noted this was the third extension and said it would not look good on Parliament; MP Tago replied that the Deputy Minister of Finance had said the NOSCA could be issued within the next 6 months.

MP Jose I. Lorena warned that the resolution must not be abused to perpetuate the accountable officers; MP Tago said 30 June 2021 is a maximum and an extension ends earlier once a regular officer is appointed.
MP Don Mustapha A. Loong, MP Jose I. Lorena and MP Baintan A. Ampatuan successively amended the title to cover the Bangsamoro Government until 30 June 2021; all were accepted.
MP Amilbahar S. Mawallil added a prayer requiring the extended accountable officers to report to Parliament at the end of their terms; accepted by MP Tago.

MP Diamila D. Ramos added public outreach duties for the public information division, public access to Parliament research, and a confidential inquiry service for MPs; accepted by MP Anna Tarhata S. Basman.

MP Maisara D. Latiph manifested that under Section 4, Rule VII the Committee on Accounts and Audit had no jurisdiction over the organizational structure, and warned she would object if it happened again; MP Baintan A. Ampatuan replied that the committee needs a settled structure as basis for allocating funds.

MP Don Mustapha A. Loong asked that the offices of the Majority and Minority Floor Leaders appear in the main organogram; MP Basman explained that officers are covered by the box of the Parliament under primus inter pares, and MP Loong yielded.
MP Don Mustapha A. Loong moved to include 2 Deputy Majority Floor Leaders and 2 Deputy Minority Floor Leaders in the structure; accepted.
MP Jose I. Lorena proposed 1 dental service position in the Medical and Health Services; accepted subject to identifying the position and salary grade.

MP Paisalin P. Tago objected to taking up the resolution because its principal author was not physically present, citing earlier cases of MP Maisara D. Latiph and MP Bai Maleiha B. Candao; the Chair inclined to follow him for fairness.

MP Nabil A. Tan moved to allow consideration and sponsorship of resolutions through Zoom, seconded by MP Maisara D. Latiph; the Majority Floor Leader said the rule was only a Speaker's guideline and the Rules would be amended in January 2021, and the measure was deferred.

items.text: MP Baintan A. Ampatuan gave sponsorship remarks and was interpellated by MPs Nabil A. Tan, Jose I. Lorena and Paisalin P. Tago; consideration was then deferred for further deliberation among MPs and the Office of the Speaker.

points.point: MP Ubaida C. Pacasem said COVID-19 restrictions left much of the 2020 budget unused and many targets unmet, and extending it to 31 December 2021 would let ministries catch up on deferred projects.
MP Edrieza H.N. Rimbang asked how much the BARMM had saved from the 2020 budget; the session was suspended and no answer is recorded.

MP Baintan A. Ampatuan questioned why an 8th placer is recognized on par with champions; MP Ziaur-Rahman Alonto Adiong said he was amenable to limiting it but the intent was to honour all who represented the country.
MP Baintan A. Ampatuan asked who would fund the activities; MP Adiong said the resolution names no source of funding for trophies or plaques.
MP Ali B. Sangki recounted handling the Qur'an Reading Competition under SPDA in 1976 and noted the honoree's name is Sundigan Magdara, not Sandigan Magdara.
MP Jamel D. Macaraya raised a point of order that the Chair had limited interpellators to 2 but recognized a third; the Chair still allowed MP Paisalin P. Tago to speak.
MP Paisalin P. Tago said he would propose monetary awards besides posthumous recognition; MP Adiong had no objection.
The Chair suggested consolidating Proposed Resolutions No. 305 and 310; MP Ziaur-Rahman Alonto Adiong explained they concern separate events in different cities, and they were approved separately.

MP Nabil A. Tan asked whether the reports would be individual and obligatory, which MP Baintan A. Ampatuan confirmed, and whether the BTA had reported to the President since 2019; she said she had seen no annual report from Parliament.
MP Nabil A. Tan and MP Jose I. Lorena urged that the requirement take effect only prospectively; MP Ampatuan said she had no problem limiting it to the 2020 report.
MP Paisalin P. Tago asked whether rice distribution and financial assistance would be highlighted; MP Ampatuan said every peso received from government should be accounted for.
MP Paisalin P. Tago suggested that the Secretariat's guidelines be submitted to Parliament for scrutiny rather than approved by the Speaker alone; consideration was deferred.

points.point: MP Musa K.S. Diamla asked whether the Committee on Agriculture had formally met and recorded the proceedings that produced the resolution; MP Ziaur-Rahman Alonto Adiong's point of order that this belonged in the Business for the Day was sustained.

MP Jose I. Lorena said he had filed a similar resolution on demarcating Bangsamoro waters in the first days of Parliament; MP Adzfar H. Usman replied that this one protects marine resources while Lorena's concerned energy resources.

MP Rasol Y. Mitmug, Jr. said that as a committee proposal it should be referred to another committee or treated as a simple resolution; the Majority Floor Leader cited the committee chair's absence and the lack of a committee report as reasons to defer.
MP Amilbahar S. Mawallil objected that this was the second time agenda items had been deferred; the Chair said deferral was the Majority Floor Leader's prerogative when the committee chair is absent.

MP Paisalin P. Tago said students learn more about Jose Rizal than the Prophet, whose life is the basis of moral governance, and told the Chair it should be a separate subject, not part of history class.
MP Romeo C. Saliga asked whether teaching it violates separation of church and state; MP Rasol Y. Mitmug, Jr. said no, since the Prophet is treated as a historical figure as well as a religious one.

MP Adzfar H. Usman and MP Baintan A. Ampatuan said it should be built into the Bangsamoro Education Code, or the legality of spending public funds on religion would be questioned; MP Saffrullah M. Dipatuan disagreed, saying waiting for the code would cause needless delay.
MP Hatimil E. Hassan proposed covering the lives of other prophets as well; MP Mitmug did not accept, saying it went beyond the committee's intent.
MP Alzad T. Sattar, MP Adzfar H. Usman and MP Maisara D. Latiph amended the title so it mandates MBHTE to include the subject in elementary, secondary, tertiary and technical education; accepted.

MP Baintan A. Ampatuan asked for an update since the resolution was filed a year earlier; MP Rasol Y. Mitmug, Jr. said the conversion could happen within the year and the resolution would encourage Congress to pass the bill.
The Majority Floor Leader called the resolution long overdue and said MP Raissa H. Jajurie supported it; MP Baintan A. Ampatuan and the Majority Floor Leader asked to be co-authors.

points.point: MP Paisalin P. Tago said Parliament should also thank President Rodrigo Roa Duterte for appointing a Bangsamoro woman to the Court of Appeals; MP Khadafeh G. Mangudadatu suggested a separate resolution for that instead.
MP Amilbahar S. Mawallil replaced the last whereas clause to call the appointment an affirmation of the Moro commitment to excellence in the judiciary; accepted.
MP Paisalin P. Tago moved to retitle the resolution to express gratitude to the President and congratulate the appointee; accepted by MP Ziaur-Rahman Alonto Adiong.
MP Maisara D. Latiph added 2 whereas clauses on the equality of women and men under the 1987 Constitution and women's participation in the State; accepted.

MP Amilbahar S. Mawallil asked what 'Bangsamoro Government' means; MP Lanang T. Ali, Jr. said it refers to the executive authority of the BTA, and offered to change it to 'Bangsamoro Transition Authority'.
MP Jose I. Lorena rejected the idea that the executive alone is the government, saying there is only one Bangsamoro Government that includes Parliament, as defined in the Administrative Code.

MP Baintan A. Ampatuan objected to dropping 'Audit' from the Committee on Accounts and Audit and asked who would review Parliament's expenditures; MP Ali said internal audit offices and the Blue Ribbon Committee cover that.

MP Laisa M. Alamia likened the Committee on Finance, Budget and Management to a Public Accounts Committee and said 'audit' was dropped because the word evoked fear; MP Ali said it was too broad and confusing.

MP Baintan A. Ampatuan's restated amendment limiting the Committee on Accounts to reviewing the Parliament budget was accepted, while MP Maisara D. Latiph's change was not accepted after consultation with the Speaker; MP Ali B. Sangki's proposal to retain 'budget' was accepted.

MP Abdulmuhmin A. Mujahid proposed adding the expenditures of the Bangsamoro Government and raising the Finance committee from 31 to 33 members; MP Ali said the first would overlap powers and the second would go to the Committee on Rules.

MP Baintan A. Ampatuan asked for a printed copy of the bill behind Committee Report No. 53 so MPs could check it with their lawyers; the Majority Floor Leader said copies would be distributed that day.

measure.titleAsRead: RESOLUTION URGENTLY DIRECTING THE MINISTRY OF HEALTH TO PROVIDE AND PRESENT A REPORT TO THE BANGSAMORO PARLIAMENT REGARDING THE ASSESSMENT, PLAN AND PROGRAM ON THE DISTRIBUTION OF COVID-19 VACCINE

items.text: Deputy Minister of Health MP Zul Qarneyn M. Abas presented the Ministry of Health's COVID-19 deployment and vaccination plan and answered questions from MPs.

points.point: MP Baintan A. Ampatuan flagged inconsistent terms for the Civil Service Commission and agencies, undefined acronyms, and strong reservations on the Bangsamoro director-general and the non-application of Career Executive Service eligibility; MP Raissa H. Jajurie agreed to make terms consistent and said third-level references were left in by inadvertence.

MP Raissa H. Jajurie said there are no third-level positions in the BARMM because these require presidential appointment, so the code instead creates second-level positions exercising executive or managerial functions.

MP Paisalin P. Tago argued the BOL lets BARMM set its own qualification standards and said he would amend the code so Shari'ah bar passers before 2014 and Mujahidin are not limited to first-level positions up to Salary Grade 9.

MP Maisara D. Latiph argued the BOL lets Parliament create its own third-level eligibility and proposed a Bangsamoro Executive Service Board for Bangsamoro third-level positions; MP Anna Tarhata S. Basman said the CES Board decree still limits that power.

MP Laisa M. Alamia asked whether current permanent third-level occupants would get new appointment papers as second-level positions; MP Basman said in practical terms yes, and noted the appeal for later consideration.

MP Laisa M. Alamia also challenged the nepotism rule's limit to the 3rd degree, the 3-month pre-election ban on reassignments, and the undefined offense of disloyalty to the Bangsamoro people; MP Basman said these were lifted from EO 292 and the 2017 RACCS and invited amendments.

MP Suharto M. Ambolodto argued the resolution only asks the Ministry of Health for a report and should be treated as a simple resolution; after MP Zul Qarneyn M. Abas and Minority Floor Leader Laisa M. Alamia agreed, MP Lanang T. Ali, Jr. withdrew his motion to refer it to the Committee on Health.
MP Omar Yasser C. Sema raised a point of order that the resolution must be approved before the Deputy Minister of Health could report; it was approved first.

MP Zul Qarneyn M. Abas reported that the BARMM was about 30% ready, vaccination was projected to start in late March or early April 2021, and the ₱500,000,000 regional allocation would serve as a buffer to vaccines supplied by the DOH.
MP Don Mustapha A. Loong proposed that the Bangsamoro Government fund the cost of adverse vaccine effects; MP Susana S. Anayatin said she would back a resolution creating a BARMM indemnity fund.

MP Laisa M. Alamia and MP Eddie M. Alih urged more vaccination sites for island areas such as Siasi, Sumisip, Mapun and Turtle Islands; MP Abas said each province has 1 refrigerated container van, so for now there would be 1 site per province.

items.text: Approved on third and final reading by nominal voting, 65 in favor, 0 against, 0 abstentions, as a bill certified urgent by the Chief Minister.
MP Lorena rendered the technical working group report on Bill No. 36 (overseas Bangsamoro workers), which was submitted for the record and set for the period of amendments on 16 March 2021.

points.point: MP Mawallil raised a point of order during the sponsorship, reminding the Body that the amended Rules allow no debate or interpellation at this stage.
MP Mangudadatu suggested that all Members be included as co-authors, which the author MP Lorena accepted.

After referral, MP Mitmug, Jr. asked whether any rule allowed the bill to pass quickly given the many co-authors; MP Ali (L), Jr. said no, and the Chair added that co-authorship does not amount to a certification of urgency.

MP Adiong asked whether the resolution's call for content 'relevant and beneficial' meant budgetary assistance; MP Ramos answered the form of support was left to the Bangsamoro Government's discretion, such as placing ministry programs on Salaam TV and Radio.
MP Tago asked what law or order created Salaam TV; MP Ramos answered it came from the President's SONA pronouncement and no Executive Order exists yet.

MP Mawallil argued the second part of the resolution set a precedent of parliamentary support for every communication initiative and was vague, and urged prioritizing the Bangsamoro Information Office budget instead.

MP Mangudadatu read 'support' as budgetary and asked that the resolution be committed to a committee; MP Ramos replied it had already been treated as a simple resolution and the support she sought was content production.
MP Rimbang supported a Salaam TV in the BARMM but said he could not support funding it, since the block grant comes from the national government.

MP Lorena moved approval subject to style; MP Adiong warned against approving measures 'subject to style', and MP Mawallil's counter-title dropping the call for support was not taken up as MP Ramos preferred MP Lorena's amendment.

MP Ampatuan voted yes 'with strong reservation' because the Code drops the Career Executive Service eligibility requirement for third-level positions, saying the BARMM should not be lesser than the ARMM.
MP Mawallil voted yes with reservations over the removed third-level standards, noting the committee accepted 12 of the 20 points in his position paper.

MP Mitmug, Jr. voted yes because review of the Code is mandatory, while listing reservations on third-level positions and the nepotism provision; MP Sattar likewise voted yes with reservation on the third-level issue.
MP Tago called his a 'progressive yes', saying the culture, heritage and religious belief of the Bangsamoro are not properly addressed by the Code.

MP Dipatuan said his amendment for the mujahideen and their families was not accepted but he yielded to a better proposition, and MP Macaraya hoped for an amendment qualifying mujahideen college graduates for salary grade 15 and up.

The technical working group recommended limiting the law's coverage to Bangsamoro territory, placing the overseas workers' help desk in POLO offices rather than embassies, and letting MOLE lawyers act only as private prosecutors under the public prosecutor.

Elected MPs Raissa H. Jajurie, Mary Ann M. Arnado, Anna Tarhata S. Basman and Jose I. Lorena as Deputy Majority Floor Leaders, and approved the chairships of 7 parliamentary and 16 statutory committees.

points.point: MP Candao supported the condolence resolutions, saying Dr. Usman had supported all her projects under her 2020 Transitional Development Impact Fund.
MP Ali (L), Jr. suggested dispensing with the period of amendments and approving the consolidated resolution subject to style, as it was only an expression of condolences.

MP Tago asked whether sessions would follow the 3 weeks a month agreed in caucus or the existing 2 weeks; MP Basman answered 2 weeks under the prevailing Rules, with a new calendar to follow new Rules.

Asked why 31 March was set as the mandatory adjournment, MP Basman said it was the last Thursday before Ramadhan; MP Tago noted the Rules do not fix an adjournment date and the Chair said the current Rules would govern.
MP Sema (OY)'s amendment changing 'Session' to 'Sessions' in the title was not accepted by MP Basman.
MP Esmael moved the mandatory adjournment from 31 March 2023 to 21 March 2023, and MP Jajurie added sessions on 27 and 29 September; both were accepted.

points.point: MP Ramos asked whether the BOL requires a list from the Council of Leaders before the Parliament passes a resolution on the Wali; MP Ampatuan said Resolution No. 1 of 2019 was the precedent and the interim government cannot rebuild every process at once.
MP Sema (OY) objected to MP Ramos calling the BOL the Members' 'bible', saying it is their basic law, and reserved his vote while awaiting the Chief Minister's position.
MP Babao countered that appointing the Wali is within the Chief Minister's exclusive power and that waiting for a Council of Leaders would be difficult since the Wali convenes the session.
MP Basman cited the Bangsamoro Administrative Code on the Wali's term; MP Ampatuan replied the Code cannot amend Section 4, Article VIII of the BOL and the first Wali's term should be 3 years.

MP Tago said the BOL's Wali provisions apply to the regular government and the BTA's Wali continues until a successor is appointed; the Chair agreed Article VIII applies once a regular government exists.

MP Ampatuan asked whether Members attending via Zoom was governed by the proposed rules; MP Dumama-Alba said they were still observing the provisionally adopted old Rules, and the Chair said video conferencing was meant to be temporary.

MP Ampatuan's proposals to delete 'as far as practicable' from the 3-day Order of Business rule and to drop the Chief Minister's written-statement option were not accepted, though her proviso that 1 vice-chairperson per committee come from the minority was accepted.

MP Ramos won new committees on Women, Youth and Children (to which MP Babao added Persons with Disabilities), but her proposed committees on Cultural Heritage, Electoral Processes and Petitions were rejected by MP Dumama-Alba.
MP Alamia's amendment changing a 2/3 vote to a simple majority and allowing video conference or hybrid sessions was accepted.
MP Dumama-Alba counter-proposed that plenary sessions start at 1 p.m., Monday to Thursday of the third and fourth week of each month, instead of MP Ampatuan's 9 a.m. proposal.
MP Mantawil added a whereas clause on Chief Minister Ebrahim's vision of 'one united Bangsamoro' and struck 'warring members of' before 'MNLF and MILF'; both were accepted.
On the first-reading bills, MPs Ampatuan and Ambolodto asked what 'Government of the Day' means as author; MP Dumama-Alba said it is defined in Section 4 of the Bangsamoro Administrative Code.

In constituting committees, MP Mendoza asked why MP Arnado was vice-chair of the Committee on Indigenous Peoples' Affairs when only 2 non-Moro indigenous people sit in the chamber, and MP Sema (R) refused membership in the Committee on Labor and Employment.

points.point: MP Lorena asked the plebiscite turnout; MP Abas (H) said 86.93% of registered voters took part, with 99.27% voting yes and 0.73% no.
MP Ampatuan and MP Lorena suggested also commending those who made the plebiscite succeed, and MP Ampatuan's amendments naming COMELEC, MBHTE, the security sectors and LGUs were accepted.
MP Sangki recalled that an earlier division creating Shariff Kabunsuan was struck down by the Supreme Court because the ARMM could not create provinces.

MP Mastura noted there is no Committee on Electoral Reform and Suffrage, and that no bills had been filed creating municipalities in the 63 SGA barangays, which he said must come before districts can be drawn in the Electoral Code.

MP Mastura asked in what capacity the Majority Floor Leader refers bills; MP Jajurie said she moves referral on the floor and the Speaker acts on it, and the Chair added unclear referrals go to the Committee on Rules.

MP Ampatuan argued that if every Member is part of the Government of the Day, interpellation of its bills should be terminated; MP Sema (OY) then raised a point of order that these matters were outside the Order of Business.

points.point: MP Baintan A. Ampatuan asked how many Bangsamoro participants competed and how the region ranked; MP Marjanie S. Macasalong said almost 2,000 students took part and only medal counts were available.
Asked by MP Baintan A. Ampatuan what government support the schools received, MP Marjanie S. Macasalong cited technical assistance through MBHTE and said the schools paid for training gyms.

MP Suharto M. Ambolodto pressed on whether any assistance, even transportation, had been given; co-author MP Amilbahar S. Mawallil said they had no concrete data but the Bangsamoro Sports Commission could still extend incentives.
MP Amilbahar S. Mawallil suggested asking the Bangsamoro Sports Commission for its list of programs while its budget was under deliberation, to inform policies on sports development.

MP Mary Ann M. Arnado asked whether commendations should carry tangible value such as a plaque; MP Diamila D. Ramos answered that incentives for achievers, such as scholarships, should be institutionalized by law.
MP Nabil A. Tan supported the resolution but suggested guidelines on the extent of commendations and congratulations the Parliament gives to achievers.
MP Omar Yasser C. Sema suggested using the full greeting “Assalamu alaikum warahmatullahi wabarakatuhu” rather than only “Salam”.
MP Froilyn T. Mendoza noted that Indigenous Peoples greet with “Fiyo bagi” or “Mauyag”, not “Salam”, and asked for an inclusive standard.
MP Omar Yasser C. Sema’s amendment, accepted by the author MP Hashemi N. Dilangalen, retitled the policy as “Assalamu Alaykum (Peace Be Upon You) and/or other culture-based greetings and smile”.
MP Eduard U. Guerra said he was disappointed the bill had not moved despite the Chief Minister certifying it as urgent and asked the Body to fast-track it.

MP Randolph C. Parcasio recalled that the MNLF peace pact shares energy revenues 50-50 and lodges license applications with the autonomous government, which recommends approval to the Department of Energy.

points.point: MP Baintan A. Ampatuan asked whether local governments such as Lanao del Sur that delivered relief had been left out; author MP Eddie M. Alih said the list was not exclusive and another resolution could recognize local officials.
MP Suharto M. Ambolodto cited the People’s Republic of China and Dinagat province as unrecognized donors; MP Mary Ann M. Arnado said records would be collated and a further resolution filed.
MP Jose I. Lorena warned that naming only some senators could make others feel like second-class citizens and suggested wording such as “all others who have given support to the BARMM”.
MP Eduard U. Guerra suggested asking the Chief Minister to write letters of thanks to everyone who helped the Paeng victims.
MP Lanang T. Ali, Jr. said the 3 victims were shot at close range, 1 bore signs of strangulation, and the parents had consented to forensic examination.

MP Amilbahar S. Mawallil asked that the resolution quote the incident report it calls deceptive; MP Lanang T. Ali, Jr. said the Lambayong police report of 2 December 2022 neither named the victims nor described them as minors.

MP Don Mustapha A. Loong warned that calling the report deceptive amounts to a Parliament finding of guilt against the police and moved to delete that clause and 3 others citing Commission powers; accepted.
MP Amilbahar S. Mawallil had the word “incidents” removed and the 4th whereas clause attributed to the witness’s account of the strangulation; accepted.

MP Jose I. Lorena asked whether ₱85,000,000,000 was the whole fiscal space; sponsor MP Ubaida C. Pacasem said it covers the block grant, tax shares, local taxes and 2020 and 2021 savings, but not projected 2022 savings.

MP Jose I. Lorena worried that extending older appropriations prolongs projects and asked about the organic law’s preference for local residents; MP Ubaida C. Pacasem pointed to procurement-law provisions in the budget since 2020.

MP Baintan A. Ampatuan argued Section 58 lets ministries modify allotments the Parliament approved; MP Ubaida C. Pacasem replied the rule was taken from the national budget and only shifts activities within a program.

MP Baintan A. Ampatuan noted ministries’ accomplishment stood at 30% from January to October and sought a mid-year review by the finance committee; MP Ubaida C. Pacasem said oversight needs no special provision and cited election, plebiscite and reappointment bans.

MP Benjamin T. Loong asked to insert ₱100,000,000 for tractors from the ₱2,000,000,000 Special Purpose Fund or ₱6,000,000,000 Contingent Fund; MP Ubaida C. Pacasem declined, saying those funds are earmarked.

MP Baintan A. Ampatuan called the MOOE-to-Capital Outlay modification a technical malversation and moved to delete it and add semi-annual review; on division of the house it lost, 17 in favor, 22 against, 3 abstentions.

rollCalls.note: Nominal voting on third and final reading, 20 December 2022; 45 in favor, none against, no abstention.
Division of the house by show of hands on MP Baintan A. Ampatuan’s proposed amendment during the period of amendments; not approved. No names recorded.

journals.presiding: Deputy Speaker Paisalin P. Tago (21 December); Deputy Speaker Sema (22 December, as printed)

attendance.note: 56 physically present and 7 virtually present at the 21 December roll call; 4 Members appeared afterwards; MPs Ahod B. Ebrahim and Pangalian M. Balindong were on official business. The session was suspended on 21 December and resumed on 22 December at 2:50 p.m. with no new roll call printed.

journals.summary: Over 2 days the Parliament passed the 2 urgent fund-extension bills: Bill No. 128, extending the 2022 Bangsamoro budget to 31 December 2023, approved 54 to 0, and Bill No. 127, extending the 2020 and 2021 Special Development Fund, stated as 53 to 0. It adopted 5 resolutions, including an appeal to reopen the DFA consular office in Cotabato City and a condemnation of the killing of Ministry of Indigenous Peoples’ Affairs official Jocelyn S. Palao, read 10 private member bills on first reading, referred 10 resolutions, and deferred Committee Report No. 01 on the Qur’an reciters resolution.

points.point: MP Baintan A. Ampatuan asked that the resolution connect to the first BTA’s earlier commendation of the same player; MP Mary Ann M. Arnado agreed and cited a Philippine Sports Commission mechanism to support young athletes.
MP Jose I. Lorena urged a program in the Bangsamoro Youth Commission or Bangsamoro Sports Commission, ideally funded in the 2023 budget, to sustain chess players in tournaments.
MP Hatimil E. Hassan proposed adding “Special Autonomous Region” after Hong Kong and “China” after Taiwan; the proponent did not accept it.

MP Omar Yasser C. Sema had the title narrowed to the Candidate Master world title and “SAR” inserted after Hong Kong; accepted, while MP Muslimin A. Jakilan’s bid to include the delegation was answered as already covered.
MP Omar Yasser C. Sema recalled that the Cotabato City consular office was a revenue-generating office and passports served as valid identification.
MP Nabil A. Tan inserted “services” after “consular” and MP Randolph C. Parcasio replaced “cater” with “serve”; both accepted.

MP Jose I. Lorena added clauses on Cotabato City as the government center and on the organic law’s provision for a Bangsamoro Pilgrimage Authority; accepted as reworded by MP Omar Yasser C. Sema to “presently hosts the government center”.
MP Eduard U. Guerra said election-year restrictions, the reappointment of Members and the Maguindanao plebiscite cost about 5 months, and the national 2022 budget already had 2-year validity.
MP Baintan A. Ampatuan explained her vote by citing the 2022 elections, the Maguindanao plebiscite and the national government’s own extension of its 2022 budget.
MP Abdulraof A. Macacua said he hesitated because of the many extensions already granted but voted yes in deference to the Body.

MP Ubaida C. Pacasem said the ₱5,000,000,000 yearly Special Development Fund reached ministries late, in the second half of 2021 for 2020 funds and the second quarter of 2022 for 2021 funds, and was further slowed by the pandemic.
MP Baintan A. Ampatuan explained that SDF approval came only in October 2021 and actual implementation of the 2020 and 2021 funds would begin in January 2023.

MP Susana S. Anayatin said they had proposed ₱10,000,000 but Congress approved ₱5,000,000 for 10 years (figures as recorded), and recounted giving capital to 100 war widows in Datu Piang and South Upi.

points.point: MP Iqbal objected that some listed sponsors should not be there, saying he did not understand why the Government of the Day would co-author a measure not certified as urgent.
Majority Floor Leader Dumama-Alba answered that the Order of Business only reflects the resolution as filed, but agreed the Government of the Day should be removed as co-author.
MP Loong (DM) said amending Bangsamoro Autonomy Act No. 7, the Bangsamoro Hymn Act of 2020, would enforce the gesture more strongly than a resolution, but supported it.

MP Mawallil noted some groups prefer to simply stand and sing and asked if that would show lack of solidarity; MP Sinolinding said the resolution only encourages the gesture and breaks no law if not followed.
MP Tago asked whether there would be penal liability for not following it; MP Sinolinding said no.

MP Lorena asked whether the closed-hand gesture would deviate from the national open-palm gesture; MP Sinolinding said the closed hand was only a suggestion and the hand stays open as in the national gesture.
MP Ramos, attending via Zoom, protested being barred from answering interpellations; the Chair said it had been ruled that no one on Zoom may respond to interpellations.
MP Ali (L), Jr. noted many Bangsamoro passed the last teachers' exam and moved to add "and all Bangsamoros who passed" to the title and body; accepted.
MP Iqbal argued many rural passengers do not fully understand English or Filipino and that using the region's 13 ethno-linguistic languages recognizes Bangsamoro identity under the BOL.

MP Tago, as MOTC Minister, supported it, saying cancellations and delays announced only in English or Filipino may not be understood, and pledged to ask airlines at Awang and Tawi-Tawi airports to use local languages.
MP Lorena amended the title so the MOTC asks the national transport department to require airline operators and airport authorities to announce in local languages; accepted by MP Iqbal.

journals.summary: Over 2 days the Parliament debated and passed the Bangsamoro Electoral Code (Bill No. 29), later Bangsamoro Autonomy Act No. 35. Debate centred on the 10,000-member requirement for regional parties, the 4% seat threshold, the 30% floor for women nominees, sectoral seats for traditional leaders and non-Moro indigenous peoples, and constitutional questions on party voting. 5 divisions of the House defeated proposals to ease those requirements, and the certified urgent bill passed on third and final reading 64 to 0 shortly before midnight on 8 March 2023.

points.point: MPs Ampatuan and Mawallil pressed for the basis of the 10,000-member requirement for regional parties; MP Dumama-Alba said it reflects over 2,000,000 registered voters and guards against fly-by-night parties, and is neither required nor barred by the BOL.

MP Lorena said the 10,000-member rule would shut out smaller groups and favour rebel fronts and existing parties, and would have set the threshold at 2.5% to 3% at first with a higher bar for coalitions, but said he had been outvoted in the Committee on Rules.

MP Ampatuan noted 30% of 40 party seats is 12, fewer than the 16 women then sitting, and with no zipper rule no women may be seated; MP Alih replied the 30% is a floor, above the 24.1% global average.

MP Mastura argued that votes for parties outside the party-list system breach Article IX-C, Section 7 of the Constitution; MP Dumama-Alba said party-list is one form of proportional representation and the Party-List Law applies only nationally.

MP Ambolodto questioned the Parliament's power to impose 6 months to 6 years' imprisonment for election offenses; MP Dumama-Alba said the penalty comes from the Omnibus Election Code and the BOL's general welfare clause allows it.
MP Tago defended the 10,000-member rule as small against a population of 4,000,000 and said fewer members would multiply parties as in the national party-list, which he said exceeded 300.

rollCalls.note: Nominal voting on third and final reading on the night of 8 March 2023: "With sixty-four (64) votes in favor, none against, and none abstention, the BTA-Parliament Bill No. 29 was passed on Third and Final Reading."

journals.presiding: Speaker Pangalian M. Balindong at the opening; Deputy Speaker Omar Yasser C. Sema from 2:18 p.m. on 20 March and on 21 March

attendance.note: Roll call on 20 March: 39 physically present and 5 virtually present (44, quorum declared); 10 more appeared virtually after roll call; 1 on official business.

journals.summary: The last sitting of the First Regular Session ran over 2 days and adjourned sine die. The Parliament read 16 bills on first reading, referred 11 proposed resolutions, and took up on second reading 8 Government of the Day bills creating municipalities in the Special Geographic Area, all referred to committees. It adopted 10 resolutions, among them thanks to Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, an inflation relief of up to 15,000 for BARMM employees during Ramadhan, committee work during recess, a 27 March 2023 holiday for the CAB anniversary, and a request that the Supreme Court integrate the Shari'ah Bar.

points.point: MP Arnado asked whether any BARMM office was ISO-certified and what it would cost; MP Dilangalen said none yet, the Ministry of Science and Technology was pursuing it, and he did not know the exact cost.

MP Lim noted quality management systems other than ISO exist and moved to change the title to certification from local or international bodies; accepted, followed by MP Arnado and MP Alih's amendments narrowing it to ministries, agencies and LGUs.
MP Ambolodto cited BARMM inflation rising from 1% to 2% in early 2022 to 7.8% in January 2023 and asked that contract-of-service and job-order workers also get 1 month's pay as relief.

MP Esmael asked about cost and capacity; MP Ambolodto estimated ₱1,200,000,000 to ₱1,400,000,000 and said the miscellaneous personnel benefit fund and the Chief Minister's contingent fund could cover it.
MP Parcasio moved to exclude MPs, ministers, deputy ministers, directors-general and heads of offices, and MP Esmael to cap the relief at 15,000 subject to available funds; both accepted.
MP Anayatin urged that a Ramadhan allowance be legislated like the 13th and 14th month pays; MP Dumama-Alba said the Government of the Day supports it but faces constraints.
MP Ampatuan asked that Members be allowed to join committee work via Zoom during Ramadhan and MP Parcasio that no meetings be held on Fridays; MP Arnado agreed to both.

MP Ampatuan and MP Loong (DM) asked about the draft rules; MP Dumama-Alba said the Bangsamoro Attorney-General's Office drafted them with Shari'ah practitioners from 2019 to 2021, and Justice Dimaampao advised first seeking a Supreme Court committee.
